page: Amazon Web Services c6g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with one thread per core, and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24286.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8581.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 969.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small blocks at 946.86 GB/sec, but drops to 169.7 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic performance is limited, with a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2187.72, though hardware-accelerated AES is supported.

The c6g.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency within the compute-optimized class due to its ARM-based Graviton architecture, which typically delivers a favorable performance-per-watt ratio compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, workloads requiring x86-specific instruction sets (such as AVX or AMX) are not supported. The instance is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, as evidenced by its average Passmark database score of 10398.82. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a medium 7B model average only 10.53 tokens per second.
